commission.name: National Security Commission on Robotics for Advanced Manufacturing (SCSP initiative; non-governmental, not a congressional/statutory body)
commission.mandate: Restore U.S. industrial preeminence by mastering the convergence of physical AI and automation; make manufacturing capacity a lasting national security asset; act as 'primary architect of a national strategy' to scale next-generation robotics.
commission.advisor_note: DLA Piper's Tony Samp is described as an official advisor (DLA Piper).
commission.duration_and_deliverables: One year; preliminary report released 2026-10-13 (~90 pages per one secondary source); final report with recommendations due March 2027.

preliminary_report.headline: America Leads in Robotics Innovation but Is Not on Track to Lead in Physical AI
preliminary_report.central_finding: U.S. leads in 'brain' technologies (AI, computer vision, autonomy, software) but lacks scale to deploy robots, produce robotic systems and manufacture critical components domestically.
key_numbers: China ~354,200 industrial robot installs in 2025 (~59% of global) vs U.S. ~38,400 (Bajraktari Substack)
Operational stock end-2024: China >2M vs U.S. 393,700 (>5x)
U.S. 8th in robot density (~307 per 10,000 mfg workers; S. Korea 1,220)
Up to 1.9M unfilled mfg jobs by 2033 (~3.8M needed); apprentices 0.3% of workforce
China ~94% of sintered permanent magnets (2024), 91% refined rare earths
National Robotics Initiative spent >$250M on 300+ projects before ending 2022
findings: Federal robotics programs spread across at least four departments with no single accountable authority
SME adoption barriers: capital, knowledge, narrow ROI metrics, cyber/liability uncertainty, lagging standards
Innovation ecosystem cannot yet scale: VC timelines fit hardware poorly, opaque concentrated supply chains, scarce data
Coordination/market failure: buyers wait for cheaper proven robots; vendors cannot cut cost without volume
preliminary_report.recommendation_status: Diagnosis, not prescriptions. Preliminary conclusion: a national mission organized around deployment; should not copy China's state-directed model or require domestic production of every component. Concrete recommendations deferred to March 2027 final report.

quotes.Bajraktari: intelligence that can't be built, deployed, and sustained at scale won't secure American industrial leadership
quotes.Budd: deploy it at the physical level across our economy
quotes.Slotkin: bring back and expand critical manufacturing processes here at home

caveats: scsp.ai/ai-robotics page itself only says 'Commission Co-Chairs' and does not name the commission; the identification comes from the March 2026 launch release.

Discrepancies: the unite.ai figures (2025 installs) and PR Newswire (2024 installs) cite different years - both given. A HyperSinc article says 'April 2026 launch' and 'Strategic Competition Support Partnership'; SCSP's release says March 17 - treat HyperSinc as erroneous.
Bajraktari is styled 'CEO' on the summit agenda and 'President' in the launch release.

scsp_work.title: The Robot Deficit: Diagnosing the U.S.-China Competition in Robotics for Advanced Manufacturing (Tech Scorecard net assessment)
scsp_work.pdf: https://scorecard.scsp.ai/content/robotics/2026/The Robotic Deficit Diagnosing US-China Robotics Net Assessment.pdf
key_points: China leads overall; U.S. retains narrow lead only in Innovation Leadership (VLA models, simulation)
China leads in Industrial Capacity, Market Ecosystem, Talent Pipeline, National Leverage; trajectory up in all five dimensions
China 54% of 2024 global installs; ~5x humanoid patent filings (page claim); projected 2.4M unfilled mfg jobs (page figure; preliminary report uses 1.9M by 2033)
U.S. imports heavily on components, lacks surge capacity; capital markets favor high-margin software over hardware; fragmented sector, no comprehensive national strategy
Scores on 1-5 scale across five categories
scsp_work.recommendations: Web page lists none specifically; syndicated coverage mentions tax incentives, federally funded programs and a dedicated government office. Full PDF not read.

scsp_work.title: Memo to the President: 10 Key Takeaways from the AI+ Robotics Summit (2024)
key_points: LLM-linked robotics; scarce real-world data and call for national database
Hardware needs capital: investment tax credits for SMEs, demand signals, defense industrial base as early market
Workforce credentialing; faster allied cooperation (Ukraine lessons); China adoption ~12x U.S. controlling for wages; no U.S. comprehensive strategy

legislation.title: National Commission on Robotics Act (H.R. 7334)
legislation.sponsor: Rep. Jay Obernolte (R-CA) with Reps. Bob Latta (R-OH) and Jennifer McClellan (D-VA)
legislation.summary: Independent 18-member commission under Commerce; interim report within 1 year, final within 2 years; scope: workforce, supply chain, manufacturing competitiveness, national security. Referred to Science/E&C/Foreign Affairs/Ed&Workforce.

legislation.sponsor: Sen. David McCormick (R-PA); cosponsors Hickenlooper (D-CO), Heinrich (D-NM), Young (R-IN)
legislation.summary: Senate companion; referred to Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Budd and Slotkin are not listed as sponsors.

legislation.title: Robotics Supply Chain Improvement Act (S. 5310)
legislation.sponsor: Sen. Mike Rounds (R-SD) with Sen. John Hickenlooper (D-CO)
legislation.summary: NIST to identify data-sharing barriers and develop robotics standards within 90 days of enactment; Commerce to report annually on robotics adoption. Referred to Commerce Committee.

legislation.title: GUARD Act (H.R. 9129)
legislation.sponsor: Reps. John Moolenaar (R-MI), Jay Obernolte (R-CA), Jennifer McClellan (D-VA)
legislation.summary: National security agencies review humanoid and quadruped robots from China and other foreign adversaries; platforms judged an unacceptable risk go on the FCC Covered List, and any not reviewed within one year are listed automatically. Referred to House Energy and Commerce; its Communications and Technology subcommittee forwarded it on 2026-09-01. A DoD-only version, Sec. 163, is in the House-passed FY2027 NDAA (H.R. 8800).

legislation.title: Humanoid ROBOT Act (S. 3275)
legislation.summary: Bars federal acquisition of foreign-made AI-integrated humanoid robots incl. from China, Iran, North Korea, Russia.

legislation.title: American Security Robotics Act (S. 4235)
legislation.sponsor: Sens. Tom Cotton (R-AR) and Chuck Schumer (D-NY); House companion Rep. Elise Stefanik (R-NY)
legislation.summary: Bars federal agencies from buying or operating unmanned ground vehicle systems (explicitly including humanoid robots and autonomous patrol technology) made by covered foreign entities such as Chinese firms; takes effect one year after enactment. Senate bill S. 4235 went to Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs on 2026-03-26. DLA Piper lists the House companion as H.R. 8189 (Stefanik); the site's policy record names Rep. Harrigan as its sponsor, so the House sponsor is unresolved.

legislation.title: Congressional Robotics Caucus (relaunched 2025)
legislation.summary: Bipartisan House caucus; goals include a national robotics strategy, international standards, worker protections. legislation.title: FCC adds foreign-produced robots and power inverters to the Covered List
legislation.sponsor: FCC, on a national security determination from an interagency body
legislation.summary: Covers mobile ground robots (autonomous mobile robots, humanoids, quadrupeds); fixed factory arms, connected vehicles, medical devices and drones are excluded. 'Foreign-produced' means anything that is not a Buy American 'domestic end product', whatever the country, so allied-made robots are covered; DoD can grant conditional approvals. Devices already authorized are unaffected.

legislation.title: Future of Defense Manufacturing Act (S. 2214)
legislation.summary: Bars DoD from buying or operating additive-manufacturing (3D printing) machines made or controlled by entities in China, Iran, North Korea or Russia, and sets up regional dual-use advanced manufacturing hubs. Slotkin's office says it was folded into the Senate FY2026 NDAA; the enacted text was not checked.

legislation.title: Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 (S. 4429; House companion H.R. 8730)
legislation.sponsor: Sens. Bernie Moreno (R-OH) and Elissa Slotkin (D-MI); House: Rep. Moolenaar
legislation.summary: Would write into statute a ban on connected vehicles, software and hardware from China and other foreign adversaries (software from 2027, hardware from 2030). Senate Commerce approved it by voice vote 2026-07-22; reports conflict on whether the full Senate has passed it, and a unanimous-consent attempt was blocked by Sen. Rand Paul.

themes.title: The deployment gap: brain vs body
themes.body: The Commission's preliminary report frames the U.S. as leading in robotics 'brain' technologies while lagging in deployment and component production, citing 2025 installs of about 354,200 in China versus about 38,400 in the U.S. The opening panel on the 'deployment moat' and the Commission report both treat deployed volume and operational data as the variable.
sessions: The Deployment Moat
Where Scale Must Start

themes.title: SME adoption and the pilot-to-scale problem
themes.body: The Commission reports that small and mid-sized manufacturers (about 95% of firms) face capital constraints, narrow ROI metrics, and cyber/liability uncertainty, and describes a coordination failure in which buyers wait for cheaper robots and vendors need volume to cut cost.
sessions: From Pilot to Scale: Trust, Return, Readiness

themes.title: Trusted supply chain, security and the China challenge
themes.body: SCSP's Robot Deficit scorecard rates China ahead on industrial capacity and national leverage; the preliminary report cites China's ~94% share of sintered permanent magnets. Pending bills (GUARD Act, Humanoid ROBOT Act, H.R. 8189) address foreign-adversary robots, and a Section 232 investigation on robotics imports remains open per available sources.
sessions: Trusted Scale: Security, Standards, & China Challenge
Federal Robotics Policy: A Demo and a Dream

themes.title: Standards and measurement
themes.body: The Commission lists lagging safety and performance standards as an adoption barrier. NIST has a draft SP 1227 on robotic assembly metrics and a humanoid baseline benchmark, and S. 5310 would direct NIST to develop robotics standards.

themes.title: The capital stack for hardware

themes.title: Workforce compact
themes.body: The Commission cites up to 1.9M unfilled manufacturing jobs by 2033 and, per Bajraktari, frames workers as essential to deployment: early operator involvement, training pathways, and success measured by safety and job quality as well as throughput.
sessions: A Robotics Compact for Workers and Industry

themes.title: Defense industrial base

people.name: Ylli Bajraktari
people.title: President & CEO
people.bio: Leads SCSP, the bipartisan nonprofit he helped found in 2021 to advise on US competitiveness in AI and emerging tech. He was executive director of the National Security Commission on Artificial Intelligence (NSCAI, 2019-2021), chief of staff to National Security Advisor H.R. McMaster, and a long-time DoD policy official (joined 2010; Afghanistan and India country director) who received the DoD Distinguished Civilian Service Medal. He co-chairs SCSP's National Security Commission on Robotics for Advanced Manufacturing with Sens. Budd and Slotkin.

In AI he has pushed a pro-adoption, light-regulation line (March 2026 'Less Hype, More Help' subcommittee hearing; FARM AI Act; letter urging CAISI to resume publishing frontier-model research). No Budd-sponsored robotics bill was found; he is not on S.4686 (National Commission on Robotics Act) or S.5310.

hill_session.title: The Hill's Robotics Agenda
hill_session.note: Paraphrased from live notes, not a transcript. These are staff remarks, not Member positions. Each point is checked against public sources; the check is shown beside it.
committees: Sen. Slotkin: Armed Services (ranking member, Emerging Threats and Capabilities), Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, Agriculture, Veterans' Affairs
Rep. Latta: Energy and Commerce; chairs the Energy subcommittee and sits on Communications and Technology, the panel that handled the GUARD Act
Rep. Obernolte: chairs Science, Space, and Technology's Research and Technology subcommittee; also on Energy and Commerce
Rep. Guthrie: chairs Energy and Commerce, which oversees the FCC and its Covered List
Commission bills: H.R. 7334 went to Science, Energy and Commerce, Foreign Affairs and Education and Workforce; S. 4686 went to Senate Commerce

points.speaker: Charlie Mlcek
points.said: Latta's district around Toledo is a very large manufacturing district with a robotics hub. Openings outnumber qualified workers, and the office expects robotics to add jobs. Latta co-chairs the Robotics Caucus.
points.check: Confirmed: Latta (OH-5) is one of four caucus co-chairs. The 86,000-jobs figure is Latta's own, from an undated statement; other sources give 60,000 to 77,000. Treat it as roughly 60,000 to 86,000.

points.topic: A national strategy from the commission, not the statute
points.speaker: Grace Kim
points.said: Congress's own commission bill is slow, so Slotkin co-chairs SCSP's commission to move first. The office hopes a national strategy comes out of its report.
points.check: Corrected: SCSP's final report is due March 2027; a preliminary report came out 2026-10-13. The statutory National Commission on Robotics Act (H.R. 7334, S. 4686) has not advanced, and the SCSP commission is not a congressional body.

points.topic: Where robots land, not just where they are built
points.speaker: Grace Kim
points.said: Every state matters, including those that only deploy robots or feel the effects, and she sees parallels to data-center pushback. She also stressed safety and trust.
points.check: Attributed opinion; nothing to check. Kim's three priorities: prepare the workforce, get security and safeguards right, and fix the messaging.

points.speaker: Charlie Mlcek
points.said: Worried about AI agents hacking deployed robots; wants an assurance and security focus for the caucus, updated privacy law (a parallel to IoT), capturing the upside and raising wages.
points.check: Attributed opinion. Related: Samp's firm published a note on Sen. Warner's draft on securing AI agents (2026-07-01). The notes also mention a Hugging Face parallel from both staffers; that point is too unclear to publish.

points.speaker: Charlie Mlcek
points.said: Backs the procurement bill Stefanik carries.
points.check: Corrected: the name is the American Security Robotics Act, not "American Strategic Security Robotics Act". Cotton and Schumer introduced it as S. 4235 on 2026-03-26 (Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs), with a House companion from Stefanik (DLA Piper: H.R. 8189). It covers federal buying and operating of Chinese-made robots, including humanoids.

points.topic: GUARD Act and the FCC Covered List
points.speaker: Charlie Mlcek
points.said: Supports the GUARD Act and FCC Covered List action to box China out. Reshoring is needed because Canada and China are treated alike. Guthrie is working on Covered List reform.
points.check: Confirmed, with context. GUARD is H.R. 9129 (Moolenaar, Obernolte, McClellan). The FCC listed foreign-produced mobile robots on 2026-07-28 and defines 'foreign-produced' as anything short of Buy American domestic content, which is why allies like Canada are caught too. Guthrie and Pallone filed a Covered List oversight bill in September 2026.

points.topic: R&D, rare earths and defense manufacturing
points.speaker: Grace Kim
points.said: Wants incentives for R&D on batteries, components and rare-earth magnets. Cited the Future of Defense Manufacturing Act from last year's NDAA, and banning Chinese vehicles.
points.check: Corrected: the Act bars DoD from Chinese-made 3D printers, not printed components. The vehicle ban is a separate bill, the Connected Vehicle Security Act (S. 4429, Slotkin and Moreno); it cleared Senate Commerce 2026-07-22 and its floor status is disputed. Magnet context: China makes about 94% of sintered permanent magnets (commission report).

points.speaker: Grace Kim
points.said: On the positive side: frontier labs doing more on security, FANUC and workforce training, and a heavy focus on jobs. The Robotics Caucus is adding staff and Mlcek solicited interest.
